item.title: Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops mindfulness of death thinking: 'May I, as long as I eat and swallow one morsel of food, attend to the…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops mindfulness of death thinking: 'May I, as long as I eat and swallow one morsel of food, attend to the Blessed One's teaching. I have done much in that way.' Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops mindfulness of death thinking: 'May I, as long as when I breathe in, I breathe out, or after breathing out, I breathe in, attend to the Blessed One's teaching. I have done much in that way.' Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is called one who dwells heedful, who sharpens mindfulness of death well for the destruction of the taints. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will dwell heedful. We will sharpen mindfulness of death well for the destruction of the taints.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.73

item.title: Elder Nun Dhīrā: Dhīrā, experience The experiences of cessation, The calming of thoughts, True happiness. Incline toward Nibbāna, The security from bondage, the unconditioned.
item.description:
Elder Nun Dhīrā:

Dhīrā, experience
The experiences of cessation,
The calming of thoughts,
True happiness.
Incline toward Nibbāna,
The security from bondage, the unconditioned.

From: Therīgāthā 1.6

item.title: By discussion, bhikkhus, a person can be known as capable or incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, evades the question…
item.description:
By discussion, bhikkhus, a person can be known as capable or incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, evades the question with another question, leads the talk outside the matter, shows anger, hatred, and displeasure — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, does not evade the question with another question, does not lead the talk outside the matter, does not show anger, hatred, and displeasure — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is capable of conversation. By discussion, bhikkhus, a person can be known as capable or incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, reviles, strikes, mocks, and seizes upon faults — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is incapable of conversation. If a person, bhikkhus, when asked a question, does not revile, does not strike, does not mock, does not seize upon faults — if this is so, bhikkhus, such a person is capable of conversation.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.67

item.title: Whatever suffering exists, All arises from nutriment. With the cessation of nutriment, There is no suffering. Knowing this danger, that suffering arises from nutriment, Fully…
item.description:
Whatever suffering exists,
All arises from nutriment.
With the cessation of nutriment,
There is no suffering.

Knowing this danger, that suffering arises from nutriment,
Fully understanding all nutriment, not depending on any nutriment,

With right knowledge, healthy, having destroyed the taints,
Using nutriment with reflection, abiding in the Dhamma,
That wise one does not fall into any category.

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.12

item.title: Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unconditioned and the path leading to the unconditioned. Listen. And what, bhikkhus, is the unconditioned? Bhikkhus, the destruction of…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unconditioned and the path leading to the unconditioned. Listen. And what, bhikkhus, is the unconditioned? Bhikkhus, the destruction of greed, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion. Bhikkhus, this is called the unconditioned. And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned? Serenity and insight, bhikkhus, are the path leading to the unconditioned.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 43.2

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, a person is shot with a dart, and they do not shoot him with a second dart. Thus, bhikkhus, that person experiences…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, a person is shot with a dart, and they do not shoot him with a second dart. Thus, bhikkhus, that person experiences the feeling of only one dart. So too, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple, when touched by a painful feeling, does not sorrow, does not grieve, does not lament, does not beat his breast, does not become confused. He experiences only one feeling: a bodily feeling, not a mental feeling. He does not feel aversion towards that painful feeling. Because he does not feel aversion, the underlying tendency to aversion towards painful feeling does not persist. Touched by that painful feeling, he does not delight in sensual pleasure. Why is that? Because the learned noble disciple knows another escape from painful feeling besides sensual pleasure. Because he does not delight in sensual pleasure, the underlying tendency to lust for pleasant feeling does not persist. He truly understands the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of those feelings. Because he truly understands the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of those feelings, the underlying tendency to ignorance for neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling does not persist. If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is unbound. If he feels a painful feeling, he feels it as one who is unbound. If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is unbound. Bhikkhus, this is called a bhikkhu who is unbound by birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is unbound by suffering.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 36.6

item.title: Elder Nādīkassapa: Truly it was beneficial for me that the Buddha came here, To the river called Nerañjarā. I heard his teaching, and my wrong…
item.description:
Elder Nādīkassapa:

Truly it was beneficial for me that the Buddha came here,
To the river called Nerañjarā.
I heard his teaching, and my wrong views were destroyed.

I performed sacrifices, recited sacrificial chants,
I kindled the sacred fire, poured offerings into the fire,
Thinking I was purified — truly I was a blind worldling.

Wandering in the forest of wrong views, blinded by rites and rituals,
Not pure, thinking I was pure — blind, I did not see.

I have destroyed wrong views, broken all existence,
I kindle the fire, worthy of offerings,
I bow down in homage to the Tathāgata, the Tamer.

All delusion is destroyed, craving for existence is shattered,
The path of birth and death is cut off; now there is no more renewed existence.

From: Theragāthā 5.6

item.title: Here, friends, while I was alone in seclusion, the following thought arose in my mind: 'Noble silence, noble silence is said. What is noble silence?'…
item.description:
Here, friends, while I was alone in seclusion, the following thought arose in my mind: 'Noble silence, noble silence is said. What is noble silence?' Then, friends, I thought: 'Here, a bhikkhu, with the stilling of initial and sustained thought, enters and abides in the second jhāna, which has internal clarity and unification of mind, without initial and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of concentration. This is called noble silence.' Then, friends, I, with the stilling of initial and sustained thought, entered and abided in the second jhāna. Friends, while I abided in this abiding, perceptions and attention accompanied by thought arose and persisted. Then, friends, the Blessed One, by psychic power, came to me and said: 'Moggallāna, Moggallāna, do not be heedless, brahmin. Regarding noble silence, establish your mind in noble silence, unify your mind in noble silence, concentrate your mind in noble silence.' Then, friends, after some time, I, with the stilling of initial and sustained thought, entered and abided in the second jhāna. Friends, one speaking rightly would say: 'The disciple attained great direct knowledge through the Teacher's assistance.' Speaking rightly, one would say of me: 'The disciple attained great direct knowledge through the Teacher's assistance.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 21.1

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as defiled with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as defiled with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would be reborn in hell accordingly.' Why is that? Because his mind is defiled. It is because of a defiled mind, bhikkhus, that some beings here, after death, with the breakup of the body, are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.43

item.title: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu practice the things proper to a samaṇa? He abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness... compassion... altruistic…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu practice the things proper to a samaṇa? He abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness... compassion... altruistic joy... equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, in all respects, he abides pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with equanimity, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will. Bhikkhus, just as a lotus pond with clear, sweet, cool, limpid water, with beautifully arranged banks, is delightful — if a person comes from the east, overcome and afflicted by heat, exhausted, parched, and thirsty, and goes to that pond, he would quench his thirst and cool his heat... if a person comes from the west... from the north... from the south... from anywhere, overcome by heat, afflicted, exhausted, parched, and thirsty, and goes to that pond, he would quench his thirst and cool his heat. So too, bhikkhus, if a person from the noble warrior caste goes forth from home to homelessness and comes to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata, and having developed loving-kindness, compassion, altruistic joy, and equanimity, attains inner concentration — I say that through this inner concentration he practices the things proper to a samaṇa.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 40 – Cūḷaassapurasutta
